newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican peso slightly weak on dollar covering.
newsitem.headline: Mexican peso slightly weak on dollar covering.

text.p: Mexico's peso opened slightly weaker against the dollar on Monday as local dealers covered their dollar positions ahead of an expected fall in local interest rates.
The 24-hour and 48-hour peso was off 0.40 and 0.25 of a centavo to 7.8655/8.870 and 7.8665/7.8720 per dollar, respectively.
Same-day contracts were down 0.20 of a centavo to 7.8610/7.8630 per dollar.
"Some banks are covering their dollar positions but the market looks quiet," one peso trader said.
Dealers said activity was thin and they expected little influence from U.S. markets.
"The peso is still strong right now; only if there were to be a very strong decrease in interest rates could it get a little shaky," a trader said.
Rates on Mexican Cetes, or T-bills, are expected to fall during Tuesday's primary auction.
